- packp.Decoder (plumbing/protocol/packp/packp.go:13) is just Decode(r io.Reader) error — so a pass-through implementation captures the RAW stream. This is what makes relay-fetch expressible without materializing into a storage.Storer.
- transport.Transport.Handshake(ctx, req) (Session, error) — pack_session.go:31

Validate that a pass-through packp.Decoder cleanly yields the pack stream on the HTTP path. smartPackSession.Command handles the v2 response-end packet; confirm that does not conflict with holding the reader open to relay bytes onward. If this does not work, item 3 below is blocked — report back before proceeding on it. Items 1, 2 and 4 are independent of the spike.

2. internal/gitproto/samesite.go (101 LOC) + guardRedirects/maxRedirects in internal/gitproto/smarthttp.go (~40 LOC) -> delete, use go-git's Handshake. Note: go-git's applyRedirect (transport/http/common.go:81) already implements git-sync's --source/target-follow-info-refs-redirect feature (adopt the redirected host for follow-up RPCs), minus the credential bug. You get the feature and the fix together.
3. HTTP fetch + ls-refs path (~300 LOC of smarthttp.go's 1021) -> Handshake + Commander.Command(ctx, "fetch"/"ls-refs", args, passthroughDecoder). Replaces RequestInfoRefs and the fetch half of PostRPCStreamBody.
4. V2Capabilities in internal/gitproto/capability.go (~50 LOC) -> Session.Capabilities()

OUT OF SCOPE — do not touch
- internal/gitproto/ssh.go: needs an SSH dialer seam in go-git that does not exist yet (sshConn is hardwired to x/crypto/ssh, and supplying your own Conn means rebuilding the command string, which is how the quoting bug happened). Upstream ask, not local work.
- The relay half of internal/gitproto/push.go: receive-pack has no protocol v2 path, so Commander cannot reach push, and Session.Push demands a storage.Storer. Needs a new PackPusher capability interface upstream.
- Keep as-is: internal/syncer, internal/planner, internal/strategy, internal/sanitize, the buffer-reusing pktline wrapper, v1 fallback, batching, progress reporting.

CONSTRAINTS
- Commander is protocol v2 only. The v1 fallback path must keep working — do not route v1 through it.
- internal/redact must stay. go-git's own redactedURL (transport/http/common.go:146) has an unfixed bug: it returns the URL verbatim when there is no password, so https://TOKEN@host/ leaks the token. Verified empirically. Do not replace git-sync's redaction with go-git's.
- Run the existing test suite (mise run test) plus the integration tests. The security regression tests added in v0.9.0 must still pass.

Report back with: spike result first, then a summary of what landed and actual LOC delta.

SPIKE RESULT: pass-through decoder works on HTTP, but the stream is only alive INSIDE Decode. That blocks the relay half of item 3, not the store half.

Verified empirically against real `git http-backend` (CGI, protocol v2), three tests:

1. PASS-THROUGH YIELDS THE RAW STREAM. `smartPackSession` does implement `transport.Commander`. `Command(ctx, "fetch", &packp.FetchArgs{...}, passthroughDecoder)` where Decode does `io.Copy(&buf, r)` captures the full v2 envelope byte-for-byte: `000dpackfile\n` + `\x01PACK\x00\x00\x00\x02...` + trailing `0006\x01\\` `0000`. Same shape git-sync's `PostRPCStreamBody` returns today, so `openV2PackStream`/`consumeV2FetchPack` would parse it unchanged.

2. THE READER IS DEAD ONCE Command RETURNS. `smartPackSession.Command` (handshake.go:276) ends with an unconditional `defer { io.Copy(io.Discard, r.resp.Body); r.resp.Body.Close() }` — the code comment says outright "Command consumes the whole response (it never streams the body out)". A decoder that reads one byte then stashes the reader gets `http: read on closed response body` afterwards. n=0.

   One trap worth knowing: if the decoder reads NOTHING, `r.resp` is still nil when the defer runs, because `httpRequester` fires the POST lazily on first Read. So a stashed reader appears to work — but the POST then executes after Command returned, outside its error handling. That's an accident, not a seam. My first cut of the test hit exactly this and gave a false pass.

3. RELAY INSIDE Decode WORKS END-TO-END. Command(fetch, decoder) → decoder strips the envelope → streams the demuxed pack into `git index-pack --stdin` in a second repo → source head resolves as a commit there. A slow external consumer is fine; nothing buffers the body.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ITEM 3 — it splits cleanly in two:

  (a) `fetchToStoreV2` and `FetchCommitParents` are ALREADY callback-shaped — both run `consumer func(io.Reader) error` inside the call. These port to `Command` directly. Unblocked, I'll take them.

Those are packages your brief says to keep as-is.

(b) is a behavior-preserving but wide refactor across three strategy packages for no security win — the two advisories were in shellQuotePath and the redirect credential re-attach, neither of which lives in the fetch relay path. `entire://` URLs are handled by the `git-remote-entire` git remote helper.

(`0002`) packet. **receive-pack** falls through to `handleConnect` (a raw
proxy): ack `\n`, banner-stripped v0 advertisement, then it reads the push

report-status, and exits. So push needs one helper process per receive-pack
RPC. The helper owns auth via the CLI's context model (`~/.config/entire/
contexts.json` → keychain `entire-core:https://<auth-host>`), NOT the legacy
`hosts.json`/`entire:<host>` scheme.

input.message:
Landed on branch worktree/silver-river-4d87, commit d62b7833. Net −99 LOC (−43 production, −56 test). Full suite + race + lint green; the 5 git-http-backend failures are pre-existing (verified identical at d4e1cfa6 in a throwaway worktree — all on the push path, "Chunked request bodies are not supported by CGI").

CORRECTION TO MY OWN LAST MESSAGE, and it is the load-bearing finding.

I told you 3(a) and 4 were coupled to item 2 because they needed a go-git Session. That was wrong. packp.CapabilityAdv and packp.FetchOutput are decoders over a plain io.Reader — no Session, no Commander, no Transport. So git-sync can adopt them while keeping its own HTTPConn and PostRPCStreamBody, which means they land on the RELAY path too, not just the store path. That is a better outcome than item 3(a) as scoped, and it does not depend on the spike at all.

WHAT LANDED
1. DecodeV2Capabilities: hand-rolled capability-advertisement walk → packp.CapabilityAdv. Only a tolerance prelude stays ours (CapabilityAdv.Decode wants "version 2" first; callers here pass whole /info/refs bodies, which over smart HTTP lead with the "# service=" banner + flush — go-git strips those in handshakeSmart, we can't reuse that).
2. consumeV2FetchPack + openV2PackStream: two copies of the v2 fetch envelope walk → one openV2Packfile over packp.FetchOutput. Also buys section-order and no-repeat validation, plus tolerance of wanted-refs and packfile-uris sections — the hand-rolled walk hard-errored on both.
3. skipV2Acknowledgments and SkipSection deleted as dead.
4. The guardRedirects comment (see below).

Error identity preserved exactly — no test error strings changed. The "ready" case reads off Acknowledgments.Ready rather than string-matching upstream's MalformedResponseError.Reason; an ERR line is caught via errors.As on *pktline.ErrorLine, which also trims better than our line[4:] did. 32 security regression tests pass (SameSite/Quote/Redirect/Auth/Withheld/Credential).

~183 lines of reimplemented grammar went away; the delta is only −99 because the replacement carries real doc comments. Judge it by what is no longer maintained, not the number.

ITEM 2 — YOUR REVISION IS RIGHT ABOUT NOT DELETING, BUT THE POSITIVE HALF STILL DOESN'T HOLD

You said "route the FETCH handshake through go-git's Handshake so that path gets go-git's redirect policy, credential clearing and cap." I did not do that, on evidence:

- go-git does NOT tighten the in-flight redirect hop. checkRedirect's own doc comment says credential handling on redirect "is left to Go's http.Client". Go's rule is shouldCopyHeaderOnRedirect → idnaASCIIFromURL → url.Hostname(). Port stripped. Verified in the Go 1.26.6 source. So the stdlib forwards Authorization from host:443 to host:9999, and go-git adds nothing there. Routing fetch through Handshake would move that path OFF our guard and onto the weaker rule — a regression, not a fix, unless we pass our own client via Options.Client (resolveClient does preserve a caller's CheckRedirect, so that composes).
- go-git clears credentials on ANY host change (redirectedURL.Host != baseURL.Host). Our sameSite deliberately allows subdomains — the doc names github.com → codeload.github.com as the case the flag exists for. go-git would drop credentials there with no credential-helper fallback.
- Handshake has no hook for the things RequestInfoRefs does: credential-helper 401 retry, pendingHelperCreds approve/reject, adoptChallengeHost, the withheld-credentials warning, StatsPhaseHeader (--stats byte accounting), httptrace, redact.Endpoint error text, content-type validation, MaxAdvertisementBytes. Options gives us Client, Authorizer, FollowRedirects, HTTPProxy, TLS, ForceDumb — and no retry seam.
- go-git's default policy is FollowInitialRedirects; our FollowInfoRefsRedirect defaults OFF. Adopting it flips a default.

So item 2's positive half is a real project with real trade-offs, not a scoping tweak. git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
gitproto: let the remote helper hold one upload-pack session open

The helper's upload-pack handler is a request loop
(githelper/stateless.go): ack, advertisement, then repeatedly read a
flush-terminated request, POST it, stream the response, emit a
response-end. One process can serve every v2 command in a run.

git-sync spawned one per RPC anyway, and since the helper re-runs
discovery on each spawn, every RPC also cost a full info/refs round trip
to the remote. A sync does the advertisement, ls-refs and at least one
fetch; a batched bootstrap does many more.

HelperConn can now hold that session open. Exposed as V2SessionConn, an
optional capability in the style of go-git's transport.Commander rather
than a widening of Conn: of the three transports only the helper can do
this — SSHConn needs a dialer seam go-git does not expose, and HTTPConn
is stateless by construction — so widening Conn would force two of three
implementors to carry a method they cannot honour. Callers type-assert
and are unaffected when the assertion fails.

The per-RPC path is untouched and stays the default; a conn that never
calls BeginV2Session behaves exactly as before. The session also steps
aside whenever the wire position stops being known: receive-pack never
rides it (its handler reads the pack until stdin EOF, so ending the
request ends the process), and a response abandoned before its
response-end drops the session rather than reusing a stream that is
mid-frame. Both fall back to a fresh process.

No change was needed to responseEndReader. It already consumes the 0002
and stops, leaving the stream positioned for the next response, so one
reader per response works on a shared stream.

Also corrects the type doc, which claimed the helper "services exactly
one stateless-connect session per process". That is false for
upload-pack and true for receive-pack, and the comment now says which is
which so neither half gets generalised onto the other.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
